name: feature-tiles
purpose: The reasons band of a marketing page: an optional centered section title over a frame grid of media tiles, each an image or an illustration above a short heading and a sentence. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-tiles', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame`, `card-grid`, `media-tile` and `illustration`. `variant` picks the layout only: `artwork` is four columns with marks on every corner, `illustrated` is three columns with marks on the bottom rule; the tiles keep the same shape in both.
useWhen: Use FeatureTiles for a static set of picture tiles.
To state three or four reasons to buy, each with a picture, under a product or pricing argument.
avoidWhen: For linked use cases or a grid of claims without pictures → use `capability-grid`.
For a scroll-driven walkthrough with one screen per feature → use `feature-scroll`.
related: `media-tile` — the picture-over-copy cell each tile is rendered with.
`feature-widgets` — the sibling band whose cells carry an action each.
bestPractices: Match the tile count to the variant: four tiles for `artwork`, three for `illustrated`.
Give a tile either `image` (a URL) or `illustration` (a registry name), not both; `scale` only matters with `illustration`.
Leave `title` empty to drop the header when the band sits under a hero that already states it; set `anchor` when a link above scrolls to the band.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Layout of the grid: `artwork` is four columns with marks on every corner, `illustrated` three columns with marks on the bottom rule.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered by the centered section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty.

props.name: tiles
props.doc: The tiles rendered as frame cells, in order; each is `{ title, description, image?, alt?, illustration?, scale? }` where `image` is a picture URL, `alt` its alternative text (empty keeps the picture decorative), `illustration` a registry name drawn fluid, and `scale` its media scale.
